A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work with the same title, authors, methods and experiments. The main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–E are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 reports original likelihood-approximation, distillation and vocabulary-trimming results. Appendix E adds DialogSum summarization and general reasoning evaluations.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix E retain these original empirical results, including the approximation plot and Tables 1–5.

M1.justification: The full-to-subset conversion, recursive Algorithm 1, beam-search approximation, sampling algorithms and distillation losses are unchanged. The revised introductory diagram does not establish a method change.

E1.justification: Both versions retain Alpaca and OPC training, GSM8K mathematical reasoning, HumanEval and MBPP coding evaluation, DialogSum summarization, and the common reasoning benchmarks in Appendix E. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1, 3–5 retain the same SFT, ALM, ULD and DSKD comparisons and their SFT combinations. DSKD remains labeled DSDK in Table 3. The added Phan et al. (2024) citation is not an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Sections 6 and Appendix E retain the model pairs, vocabulary sizes, data splits, shot counts, loss weights and training settings. The edit from 'average maximum length of 10' to 'average length of 10' does not specify a changed beam-search limit or procedure.

E4.justification: The approximation-quality check in Figure 4 and comparisons across vocabulary sizes and loss combinations are retained unchanged. No ablation, robustness test, sensitivity analysis or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. There is no change in uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 and Figure 4 retain the same results, including SFT + PKL's 55.6 GSM8K accuracy, 33.9 DialogSum ROUGE-L and the approximation RMSE of 0.015. Figure 1's changed example probabilities are illustrative labels, not revised experimental results.

T1.justification: Definitions 1–4, Lemmas 1–2, the derivations and appendix proofs are unchanged. Example 4's equations lose their numbers, shifting subsequent equation references without changing the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about exact subset scoring with O(1) model evaluations, general BPE conversion, and distillation and memory benefits. Local wording edits do not change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: The computational-cost caveats, pruning rationale, whitespace-based approximation assumptions, result interpretations and future directions are retained. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added.

D1.justification: The v2 abstract adds a concrete code-repository address, whereas v1 provides only a future artifact-release statement. Implementation and training details otherwise remain unchanged; the PDFs alone do not establish the repository's accessibility or completeness.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds a citation and discussion of Phan et al. (2024), acknowledging partial exploration of cross-tokenizer conversion under maximum-prefix encoding and distinguishing that setting from BPE. The remaining research positioning is preserved.

P1.justification: There are localized edits to the abstract, introduction, algorithm overview and related-work prose, plus an acknowledgment and an ICLR 2026 publication header. The main section sequence and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 replaces the 'Distill models fast?' example with 'cross-vocab distillation' and revises its token and probability labels. Figure 3 moves from page 6 to page 5, Table 3's caption is edited, and closing statements move to a separate page. Experimental displays retain their content and structure.

improvement.justification: The added code pointer improves implementation-access information, and the maximum-prefix discussion makes the relationship to earlier research more explicit. These are limited, supported gains; the methods, proofs and empirical evidence remain unchanged, and repository availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.
